subject: Re: [unmarked] gmultmix mixture=P or NB: equivalent estimates?

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] gmultmix mixture=P or NB: equivalent estimates?
parts:
Hi Michael,

Yes, everything looks correct. Note that lambda=E[N] for the Poisson and NB distributions (at least for this particular parameterization of the NB). So, the estimates of lambda should be the same for both models, and they both should be close to 10 in your example, as they seem to be. For the NB model, you get an estimate of the overdispersion parameter, which should be close to 0.5. This bit of code may help clarify how different these two models actually are:

Nc <- 0:100
hist(N, freq=FALSE, breaks=seq(0, 100, 5), ylim=c(0, 0.15))
lines(Nc+0.1,
      dpois(Nc, exp(coef(fit.P, type="lambda"))),
      col=2, type="h")
lines(Nc+0.2,
      dnbinom(Nc, mu=exp(coef(fit.NB, type="lambda")),
              size=exp(coef(fit.NB, type="alpha"))), col=4, type="h")


Richard


On Thu, Nov 15, 2012 at 2:06 PM, msm <michael...@gmail.com> wrote:
For an NB generated abundance mixture with a binomial removal process, gmultmix w/o covariates returns equivalent estimates for several parameters when the mixture is assumed to be NB, or is assumed to be P.  Is this correct?

In the example below, the NB mixture generator has mean=10, variance=210, and resembles an exponential distribution (i.e., clearly not Poisson).  In this case, at least, the estimates assuming P or NB are the same for lambda, p, var(p), cov(lambda,p).  Only var(lambda) differs.

# =============================================================================

  library( unmarked )

  I <- 100
  J <- 3
  p <- 0.5

  N <- rnbinom( I, mu=10, size=0.5 )

  X <- matrix( NA, nrow=I, ncol=J )
  Z <- N
  for ( j in 1:J ) {
    X[,j] <- round( rbinom( I, Z, p ) )
        Z <- Z - X[,j]
  }

  X.umf <- unmarkedFrameGMM( X, numPrimary=1, type="removal" )

  fit.P  <- gmultmix( ~1, ~1, ~1, X.umf, "P" , control=list( reltol=.Machine$double.eps ) )
  fit.NB <- gmultmix( ~1, ~1, ~1, X.umf, "NB", control=list( reltol=.Machine$double.eps ) )

  coef( fit.P )
  coef( fit.NB )

  vcov( fit.P )
  vcov( fit.NB )

# =============================================================================

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] gmultmix mixture=P or NB: equivalent estimates?
parts:
Thanks Richard,

It’s interesting that the mixture distribution assumption (P or NB) doesn't affect the likelihood wrt lambda.  Is this related to the fact that for an iid sample from each of these distributions, the mle of the distribution expectation is the sample mean for both the P and NB, and that for the NB the covariance of the mles for "lambda" and "alpha" are asymptotically 0?

It’s also interesting that the detection (capture) probability point and variance estimates are identical under the P and NB mixture assumption.  Seems like it should depend on the unit-specific estimated abundances, which would differ between P and NB?  I'm guessing, given that the estimated "lambda" are identical, that the information in the data related to the estimation of the capture probability is limited to the magnitude of the capture data relative to the estimated "lambda", and doesn't involve the variation in abundance among sample units per se (estimated cov(p,alpha) near 0)?  Is the estimate of q broadly invariant to the assumed mixture distribution, or just when its assumed to be either P or NB?

Michael
